question.problem: Vehicles arrive at a crossing continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one every $10$ seconds. Determine the probability that the next vehicle will arrive at the crossing within the next $3$ seconds. Round your answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Since the time intervals between the arrival of two successive vehicles at the crossing are continuous and independent, and arrivals occur at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next vehicle arrives as an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the time between the arrival of two successive vehicles at the crossing. Then, since vehicles arrive every $10$ seconds on average, the rate is $\lambda =1/10$ vehicles per second.

The time between arrivals can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =1/10,$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{10}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10}{e}^{-x/10}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the next vehicle will arrive at the crossing within the next $3$ seconds is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<3) & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{10}{e}^{-x/10}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-{e}^{-x/10}|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =-{e}^{-3/10}+{e}^{0} \\  & =1-{e}^{-3/10} \\  & ≈0.2592\end{aligned}
$$
